te-iru.meaning: is doing ...; a state that keeps going
te-iru.note: With action verbs it means "is doing" (食べている). With words like marry, live and know it is a state (結婚している = is married).

te-kudasai.note: A polite request. More polite: 「〜てくださいませんか」.

naide-kudasai.note: Verb ない form + でください.
naide-kudasai.translation: Please do not take photos here.

te-mo-ii.meaning: it is okay to ...; you may ...
te-mo-ii.note: The question 「〜てもいいですか」 asks for permission.

te-wa-ikenai.meaning: must not ...; it is forbidden to ...
te-wa-ikenai.note: In speech it is often shortened to 「〜ちゃいけない」 or 「〜じゃだめ」.

nakereba-naranai.note: Also said 「〜なくてはいけない」. In speech it is shortened to 「〜なきゃ」 or 「〜なくちゃ」.
nakereba-naranai.translation: I have to take medicine every day.

nakute-mo-ii.meaning: it is okay not to ...; no need to ...
nakute-mo-ii.note: The opposite in meaning of 「〜なければならない」.
nakute-mo-ii.translation: You don't have to come tomorrow.

tai.note: States your own wish. For other people, use 「〜たがる」 or 「〜たいそうだ」.
tai.translation: I want to drink some iced water.

tagaru.note: Describes a wish that a third person shows. Often 「〜たがっている」.
tagaru.translation: The child wants to play outside.

mashou.note: Invites the other person to do something together, or states a decision.

mashou-ka.note: Offers to help, or checks with the other person.

masen-ka.note: A more polite invitation than 「〜ましょう」.
masen-ka.translation: Would you like to watch a movie together?

ta-koto-ga-aru.note: Talks about a past experience. 「〜たことがない」 means have never done it.

koto-ga-aru.note: Follows the dictionary form or the ない form. Different from 「〜たことがある」 (an experience).

tari-tari.note: Gives a few examples out of several things, and usually ends with 「する」.
tari-tari.translation: On days off I read books, watch movies and so on.

mae-ni.note: The verb is in the dictionary form, whether the whole sentence is past or present.
mae-ni.translation: I brush my teeth before going to bed.

ta-ato-de.note: The verb is in the た form.
ta-ato-de.translation: I take a walk after eating.

te-kara.note: Stresses the order: finish the first thing, then do the second.
te-kara.translation: I'll play after I finish my homework.

nagara.note: One person does two things at the same time, and the main action goes last.
nagara.translation: I study while listening to music.

ga-hoshii.note: Use 「〜がほしい」 for wanting things and 「〜たい」 for wanting to do things.

ni-iku.note: Verb ます stem + に + 行く/来る, showing the purpose.
ni-iku.translation: I'm going to the library to borrow books.

deshou.note: 「でしょう」 is polite and 「だろう」 is the plain form. With a rising tone at the end it confirms: "right?".

kara-reason.note: The speaker's own reason. It can be followed by a command or a request.
kara-reason.translation: It's raining, so I won't go out.

node.note: More objective and softer than 「から」. Often used to explain reasons and to apologize.
node.translation: Because it is raining, I won't go out.

noni.note: The result is the opposite of what was expected, often with dissatisfaction or regret.
noni.translation: I studied a lot, yet I did not pass the exam.

ga-but.note: Connects two contrasting things. It can also be just an opener (すみませんが).
ga-but.translation: This shop is expensive, but the food is good.

kedo.translation: I want to go, but I have no time.

toki.note: Noun + の + とき, な-adjective + な + とき, and verbs and い-adjectives connect directly.
toki.translation: When I was a child, I often played in the river.

mada-te-inai.note: Used when answering 「もう〜ましたか」.

tsumori.note: A plan already decided. 「〜ないつもり」 means plan not to ....
tsumori.translation: I plan to go to Japan next year.

hou-ga-ii.meaning: had better ...; it is better to ...
hou-ga-ii.note: Gives advice to someone, and the verb is often in the た form.
hou-ga-ii.translation: You had better sleep a bit more.

yori-hou-ga.note: AよりBのほうが〜: B is more ....

ichiban.note: Picks the top one out of three or more things.
ichiban.translation: Among fruits, I like apples best.

shika-nai.note: Always followed by a negative, with a feeling of "too little". 「だけ」 has no such feeling.
shika-nai.translation: I have only a thousand yen in my wallet.

amari-nai.translation: This apple is not very tasty.

zenzen-nai.translation: I don't understand Japanese at all.

ga-suki.meaning: like / dislike / be good at / be bad at ...
ga-suki.note: The target of these words takes 「が」, not 「を」.

naru.note: Nouns and な-adjectives take 「になる」, and い-adjectives change to 「〜くなる」.

ni-suru.note: Often used when ordering or choosing: 「コーヒーにします」.

dake.note: Simply limits the range, with no feeling of "too little".

no-desu.note: Explains a situation, asks for a reason or adds stress. In speech it is 「〜んです」.

te-aru.meaning: has been done (by someone) and stays that way
te-aru.note: Someone did something on purpose and the result remains. The object usually takes 「が」.
te-aru.translation: The window is open (someone opened it).

te-oku.meaning: do ... in advance; leave it as it is
te-oku.note: Prepares for later, or keeps things as they are. In speech it is 「〜とく」.
te-oku.translation: I book the hotel before the trip.

te-shimau.note: Shows something done completely, or with regret. In speech it is 「〜ちゃう」 or 「〜じゃう」.

te-miru.translation: May I try on this clothing?

te-iku.note: A change that continues from now into the future, or moves away from the speaker.
te-iku.translation: It will get colder and colder from now on.

te-kuru.meaning: start to ...; gradually ... (up to now); come ...ing
te-kuru.note: A change that has continued from the past to now, or that comes toward the speaker.

te-ageru.note: I (or someone on my side) do it for someone else. Said directly to an elder, it can sound condescending.
te-ageru.translation: I bought a book for my younger sister.

te-kureru.note: Someone does it for me (or my side), with thanks. More polite: 「〜てくださる」.
te-kureru.translation: A friend took me to the station.

te-morau.meaning: have someone do ... for me; receive ...
te-morau.note: The person who does it takes 「に」. More polite: 「〜ていただく」.

te-hoshii.note: The person who does it takes 「に」.
te-hoshii.translation: I want you to speak a bit more slowly.

tara.note: The most widely used "if", and it can also mean "after ... has happened".
tara.translation: Please call me when you get to the station.

ba.note: When the condition is met, the result follows. It focuses on the condition itself.
ba.translation: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

to-cond.meaning: as soon as ...; if ... then inevitably ...
to-cond.note: A natural or inevitable result. It cannot be followed by a command, a request or a will.
to-cond.translation: When spring comes, it gets warm.

nara.note: Picks up what the other person said or the topic, and gives advice.
nara.translation: If you are going to Japan, Kyoto is nice.

temo.translation: I'll go even if it rains.

you-ni-naru.meaning: come to be able to ...; begin to ...
you-ni-naru.translation: I have become able to speak Japanese.

you-ni-suru.note: 「〜ようにしている」 means you keep paying attention to doing it.
you-ni-suru.translation: I try to eat vegetables every day.

you-ni.note: Usually follows an ability, a natural change or a negative (忘れないように). For things you want to do, use 「ために」.
you-ni.translation: I write it down so that I don't forget.

you-ni-iu.note: Reports a command or request: 〜ように言う／頼む／伝える.
you-ni-iu.translation: The teacher told the students to be quiet.

you-da.note: A guess from what you saw or heard. 「みたいだ」 is more casual.

koto-ni-suru.note: A decision you make yourself. 「〜ことにしている」 is a rule you set for yourself.
koto-ni-suru.translation: I decided to run every morning from next year.

koto-ni-naru.meaning: it is decided that ...; it turns out that ...
koto-ni-naru.note: Not decided by oneself alone, or the result of how things went.
koto-ni-naru.translation: I am going to move to Osaka next month.

koto-ga-dekiru.note: A little more formal than the potential form (弾ける).

sou-looks.note: Follows a verb ます stem or an adjective stem (高そう), and is how something looks to your own eyes.
sou-looks.translation: It looks like it is going to rain.

sou-hear.note: Follows the plain form (雨だ、降る), and is something heard from someone else.
sou-hear.translation: I hear it will rain tomorrow.

rashii.note: A guess from news you heard, and the speaker does not take much responsibility.
rashii.translation: I hear that shop is closing next month.

kamoshirenai.note: A possibility of about half or lower.

hazu.note: A conclusion drawn from reasoning or fact, with strong confidence.

hazu-ga-nai.translation: He can't possibly have said such a thing.

nasai.note: A command from a higher person to a lower one, such as parent to child or teacher to student.

saseru.note: Causative: make someone do something, or allow someone to do it.
saseru.translation: Mother made the child eat vegetables.

sasete-kudasai.note: Asks the other person to allow you to do something.
sasete-kudasai.translation: Please let me take a rest.

rareru-passive.meaning: be ...ed; can also mean "can ..." or be honorific
rareru-passive.note: Godan verb + れる can only be passive or honorific. Ichidan verb + られる can also mean "can". It often has a feeling of being harmed.
rareru-passive.translation: The cake was eaten by my younger brother.

saserareru.note: Causative + passive: someone makes you do something you don't want to do.
saserareru.translation: I was made to learn the piano as a child.

you-to-omou.note: States your own thought or plan, more like something you have just thought of than 「つもり」.
you-to-omou.translation: I am thinking of going to Japan next year.

you-to-suru.note: An action is about to begin, or you make an effort to do it.
you-to-suru.translation: Just as I was about to go out, it started to rain.

to-omou.translation: I think it will clear up tomorrow.

to-iu.note: Introduces a name or content: 「さくらという店」.
to-iu.translation: Do you know a shop called "Sakura"?

tame-ni.note: When the front part is an action you control, it means "in order to". When it is an event, it is the cause.
tame-ni.translation: I came to Japan to study Japanese.

sugiru.note: Follows a verb ます stem or an adjective stem.

yasui-nikui.note: Follows a verb ます stem. 「〜づらい」 also means hard to ....
yasui-nikui.translation: This book has big print and is easy to read.

kata.translation: Please teach me how to read this kanji.

hajimeru.note: Follows a verb ます stem. 「〜出す」 means to start suddenly.

shi.translation: This shop is cheap and tasty, so I come often.

ka-dou-ka.note: Puts a yes-no question inside a sentence.
ka-dou-ka.translation: I don't know whether he will come.

tokoro.meaning: just about to ... / in the middle of ...ing / have just ...
tokoro.note: Dictionary form + ところ: about to; ている + ところ: in the middle of; た + ところ: just now.
tokoro.translation: I'm just about to go out.

ta-bakari.note: The speaker feels not much time has passed.
ta-bakari.translation: I have only just come to Japan.

uchi-ni.note: Do it before the state changes.
uchi-ni.translation: I want to visit various countries while I'm young.

aida-ni.note: 「間」 is the whole period and 「間に」 is a moment within that period.
aida-ni.translation: A thief broke in while we were away from home.

mama.note: A state that should have changed did not change.
mama.translation: I fell asleep with the window open.

zu-ni.note: Means the same as 「〜ないで」 and is more written. 「する」 becomes 「せずに」.
zu-ni.translation: I went to school without eating breakfast.

naide.note: Does another thing in a state of not doing something.
naide.translation: I went out without an umbrella.

o-ni-naru.note: Raises the other person's action: お + ます stem + になる.
o-ni-naru.translation: The teacher has already gone home.

o-suru.note: Lowers oneself and does something for the other: お + ます stem + する／いたす.

ni-tsuite.note: The content of talking, thinking or investigating.

ni-yotte.note: Also used in passive sentences to show who did it (by ...).
ni-yotte.translation: Ideas differ from person to person.

ni-yoru-to.note: Explains the source of news, and the sentence often ends with 「そうだ」 or 「らしい」.
ni-yoru-to.translation: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.

ni-totte.note: Judges from someone's point of view.
ni-totte.translation: For me, family is the most important.

ni-taishite.note: The target of an action or attitude. It can also show a contrast.
ni-taishite.translation: He is very polite to his elders.

ni-kanshite.translation: I have a question about this matter.

ni-kurabete.translation: Compared with last year, this year is hot.

ni-chigainai.note: A guess the speaker is very sure about.

ni-suginai.note: Stresses that the degree is very low or unimportant.
ni-suginai.translation: That was nothing more than a joke.

wake-da.note: Draws a natural conclusion from the facts just mentioned.
wake-da.translation: He practices every day, so no wonder he is so good.

wake-ga-nai.translation: There's no way it is that easy.

wake-dewa-nai.note: A partial denial that corrects what the other person may think.
wake-dewa-nai.translation: It's not that I dislike eating meat.

wake-ni-wa-ikanai.note: You cannot do it because of reason or social common sense. With a negative in front it means "cannot not do".
wake-ni-wa-ikanai.translation: I promised, so I can't not go.

beki.note: What the speaker thinks is right or a duty. 「〜べきではない」 means should not.

toori.note: When it follows a noun directly, it is read 「どおり」.
toori.translation: I wrote it as the teacher said.

tabi-ni.translation: Every time I hear this song, I remember my hometown.

okage-de.translation: Thanks to my teacher, I passed.

sei-de.translation: I was late because of the rain.

kuse-ni.note: Carries blame or contempt, stronger than 「のに」.
kuse-ni.translation: Even though you know, you don't tell me.

ba-hodo.note: The same word is repeated: 〜ば〜ほど.
ba-hodo.translation: The more I think about it, the more confused I get.

hodo-nai.note: AはBほど〜ない: A is not as ... as B.
hodo-nai.translation: This year is not as cold as last year.

ba-yokatta.note: Regret about something not done in the past.
ba-yokatta.translation: I wish I had left home earlier.

tara-dou.note: Gives a suggestion to the other person, fairly casually.

to-ieba.note: Reminds you of something representative of the topic.
to-ieba.translation: Speaking of Japan, it is Mt. Fuji, isn't it?

to-iu-no-wa.note: Explains the meaning of a word, and the sentence often ends with 「〜ことだ」.
to-iu-no-wa.translation: "Tsundoku" means buying books and not reading them.

tte.note: Spoken, equal to 「と」, 「という」 and 「そうだ」.
tte.translation: I hear tomorrow is a holiday.

nante.translation: To think he is getting married, I can't believe it.

sae.translation: I'm so busy I don't even have time to eat.

koso.translation: This year I will pass the Japanese test for sure.

demo-even.note: Gives one example, and all the others go without saying.
demo-even.translation: Even a child understands this problem.

bakari.note: Carries dissatisfaction that there is too much. 「〜たばかり」 has another meaning (just now).
bakari.translation: My younger brother only plays games.

shika-nai-verb.note: Dictionary form + しかない: there is no other way.
shika-nai-verb.translation: There are no more buses, so I have no choice but to walk home.

koto-da.meaning: it is (the matter of) ...; it is best to ...
koto-da.note: Often used to explain "... means doing something". When giving advice it means "it is best to ..., you should ...", depending on the context.
koto-da.translation: If you want to get good, you should practice every day.

mono-da.note: Remembers a habit of the past.
mono-da.translation: As a child I often swam in this river.

ppoi.note: Spoken, often with a negative meaning: 子供っぽい (childish), 忘れっぽい (forgetful).
ppoi.translation: This outfit is a bit childish.

gachi.translation: You tend to catch colds in winter.

kke.note: Spoken, used to check with the other person when you cannot remember.
kke.translation: What time did the meeting start again?

ni-shite-wa.note: The result differs from what common sense would suggest.
ni-shite-wa.translation: For a first time, you did very well.

tsumori-de.note: You thought you had done it, but may not have.
tsumori-de.translation: I thought I had locked the door, but it was open.

dake-de-naku.translation: He can speak not only English but also Chinese.

nagara-mo.note: Written style. The two things seem to contradict each other.
nagara-mo.translation: Although small, it is a happy home.

te-tamaranai.note: A feeling or emotion that is extremely strong.
te-tamaranai.translation: I can't stand how hot it is.

te-shikata-ga-nai.note: A strong emotion or feeling that you cannot control.
te-shikata-ga-nai.translation: I'm extremely worried about the exam result.

sae-ba.note: This one condition alone is enough.
sae-ba.translation: As long as I have time, I want to travel.

ni-mo-kakawarazu.note: The front situation would normally prevent the back event, but it happened anyway. More written and formal than 「のに」.
ni-mo-kakawarazu.translation: In spite of the rain, the match was held.

zaru-wo-enai.note: You do not want to, but have no other way. Verb ない form minus ない + ざる; する becomes せざる.
zaru-wo-enai.translation: It is my boss's order, so I have no choice but to obey.

dake-atte.meaning: as one would expect from ...; precisely because ...
dake-atte.note: The status or effort in front matches the result behind it, with a tone of praise.
dake-atte.translation: As you would expect from a singer, she sings really well.

ta-totan.note: The second thing happens right after the first, and is often unexpected.
ta-totan.translation: The moment I finished eating, I felt sleepy.

ta-ue-de.note: First finish the front thing, and then do the next on that basis.
ta-ue-de.translation: I'll decide after hearing the explanation.

ni-kawatte.note: Someone else does it in place of the person who should.
ni-kawatte.translation: I will give the speech on behalf of the president.

muke.note: Follows a noun and shows it is made especially for that kind of person or target.
muke.translation: This is a book for children.

ni-mukete.note: Works or prepares toward a goal or direction.
ni-mukete.translation: I study every day for the exam.

gatai.note: Hard to do for emotional reasons. Follows a verb ます stem. More written than 「〜にくい」.
gatai.translation: His words are hard to believe.

kanenai.note: A bad result could happen, and the speaker is a bit worried. Note that 「〜かねる」 means "cannot ...".
kanenai.translation: A person like that could even do such a thing.

mono-ka.note: A strong denial with emotion. In speech it is often 「もんか」.
mono-ka.translation: As if I'd know a thing like that!

kkonai.note: Spoken, a very firm denial. Follows a verb ます stem.
kkonai.translation: No matter how much you beg him, he will never come.

wari-ni.note: Judging from the front condition, the result is not what you would normally expect.
wari-ni.translation: It is not tasty for the price.

kara-koso.note: Stresses the reason: this reason and no other.
kara-koso.translation: Precisely because I'm busy, I should watch my health even more.

bakari-ka.note: Not just the first thing, but also the second, which goes even further.
bakari-ka.translation: He can speak not only English but also Chinese.

ni-kagiru.note: The speaker thinks this is the best choice.
ni-kagiru.translation: In summer, beer is the best.

ni-kagirazu.note: Not just what was said, the others are the same.
ni-kagirazu.translation: This shop is crowded not only on weekends but always.

wo-hajime.note: Names the most representative one first, then the others of its kind.
wo-hajime.translation: Starting with Tokyo, prices are high in big cities.

wo-moto-ni.note: Uses the front thing as material or grounds.
wo-moto-ni.translation: A film was made based on the facts.

ni-sotte.note: Follows a policy or plan. It can also mean along a river or road.

ni-motozuite.note: Uses the front thing as the basis. More formal than 「をもとに」.
ni-motozuite.translation: A judgment is made based on the law.

shidai.note: Once the first thing is done, do the second at once. Follows a verb ます stem.
shidai.translation: We will leave as soon as we are ready.

kiri.note: After doing this, the situation has not changed.
kiri.translation: I met him once last year and haven't seen him since.

ppanashi.note: Does something and then leaves it, often with a tone of criticism.

you-ga-nai.note: Even if you want to, you have no means to. Follows a verb ます stem.
you-ga-nai.translation: I don't have his contact details, so there's no way to tell him.

ka-no-you-ni.note: It is not actually so, but someone acts as if it were.
ka-no-you-ni.translation: He talks as if he knew nothing.

osore-ga-aru.meaning: there is a risk of ...; may ...
osore-ga-aru.note: Something bad could happen. Often used in news and weather forecasts.
osore-ga-aru.translation: There is a chance a typhoon will come.

mono-no.note: Admits the front matter, but the result behind is not what you would expect.
mono-no.translation: I said I would go, but I haven't prepared yet.

tsutsu.note: Written style. Shows two things at once, or "although I know ..., ...". 「〜つつある」 means "is gradually ...ing".
tsutsu.translation: Though I knew it was wrong, I told a lie.

koto-wa-nai.note: It is not necessary to do so, often used to comfort or advise someone.

nai-koto-wa-nai.note: A double negative: not completely impossible, but not eager either.
nai-koto-wa-nai.translation: It's not that I can't eat it.

ni-kimatte-iru.note: A judgment the speaker is very sure about, common in speech.

te-naranai.note: A feeling or sensation wells up naturally and cannot be controlled. Close to 「〜てたまらない」.

zu-ni-wa-irarenai.note: You cannot control yourself and will surely do it.

te-bakari-iru.note: Always does only this one thing, often with dissatisfaction.

tsuide-ni.meaning: while at it; on the way
tsuide-ni.note: While doing one thing, you also do another.
tsuide-ni.translation: I stopped by the post office on my way to shop.

saichuu.translation: The phone rang in the middle of the meeting.

ippou-da.note: A change goes in only one direction, mostly a bad change.

koto-ni-feeling.note: Says the speaker's feeling first, then the matter. Follows feeling words: 残念な、驚いた、嬉しい.

ni-shite-mo.note: Even in this case, the rest is the same.
ni-shite-mo.translation: Even if you go, please get in touch.

ni-seyo.note: In any case, the conclusion is the same. A little more written than 「にしても」.

wa-mochiron.note: The front is natural, and the back is the same.
wa-mochiron.translation: I can speak English, of course, and French too.

wa-tomokaku.note: Puts the front aside and talks only about the back.
wa-tomokaku.translation: Price aside, the taste is good.

bakari-ni.note: Because of this one reason alone, the result turned bad, with regret.
bakari-ni.translation: Just because I told the truth, I got scolded.

ue-wa.note: Since things have come to this, you must see it through. Written style.
ue-wa.translation: Now that I've accepted it, I must do it to the end.

n-bakari.note: It looks as if it is just about to happen (but it does not). Verb ない form minus ない + んばかり.
n-bakari.translation: He had a look that said "Go away!"

wo-mono-tomo-sezu.note: Not afraid of difficulty or danger and goes ahead bravely. Mostly used in praise of others.
wo-mono-tomo-sezu.translation: Undaunted by his injury, he played in the match.

tomo-naru-to.note: Once you reach such a position or level, it naturally goes like this.
tomo-naru-to.translation: Being a company president, you must be busy.

to-ittara-nai.note: The degree is so high that words fail. Spoken.

zukume.note: The surroundings are all the same kind of thing, mostly good things, and also black clothes (黒ずくめ).
zukume.translation: Today was nothing but good things.

meku.meaning: looks like ...; has a touch of ...
meku.note: Takes on a certain feeling or air. Common: 春めく, 謎めく, 皮肉めいた.
meku.translation: It is slowly starting to feel like spring.

nagara-ni.note: Stays in its original state. Common: 生まれながら, 涙ながら, 居ながらにして.
nagara-ni.translation: She was born a good singer.

ga-hayai-ka.note: The second thing happens almost at once after the first. Written style.
ga-hayai-ka.translation: No sooner had the bell rung than the students rushed out of the classroom.

nari.note: Right after the first action, an unexpected second action follows. The subject is the same person (third person).
nari.translation: As soon as he got home, he fell asleep.

soba-kara.note: Just after finishing, it is spoiled again and again, with a feeling of helplessness.
soba-kara.translation: As soon as I tidy up, the children make a mess again.

ni-itatte-wa.translation: As for my younger brother, he has never helped even once.

wo-kawakiri-ni.note: Begins here and keeps developing from then on.
wo-kawakiri-ni.translation: Starting in Tokyo, they hold concerts all over the country.

atte-no.note: Only because the front exists can the back hold.
atte-no.translation: Without customers there is no business.

ni-katakunai.note: Written style. Easy to imagine or understand. Common: 想像にかたくない, 察するにかたくない.
ni-katakunai.translation: It is not hard to imagine how hard it was for him.

te-yamanai.note: A feeling that continues and is very strong. Common: 願ってやまない, 愛してやまない.

wo-kinjienai.note: Written style. A feeling wells up naturally and cannot be controlled.
wo-kinjienai.translation: I couldn't help being surprised to hear the news.

mono-wo.note: It would have been good if it had been done that way, with regret or blame.
mono-wo.translation: If you had said so earlier, I would have helped you.

to-atte.note: Because of this special situation, it naturally goes this way.
to-atte.translation: Because it is a long weekend, the roads are jammed.

made-mo-nai.note: The matter is clear and there is no need to do it.
made-mo-nai.translation: You don't even need to say such a thing.

dewa-arumaishi.note: It is not that kind of situation, so you should .... Advice or criticism often follows.
dewa-arumaishi.translation: You're not a child, so do it yourself.

zu-ni-wa-okanai.note: Naturally causes some result, or the speaker is determined to do it.
zu-ni-wa-okanai.translation: His work is bound to move people.

nai-to-ikenai.note: Means the same as 「〜なければならない」 and is more spoken. Saying just 「〜ないと。」 also has this meaning.

jan.note: Spoken form of 「じゃないか」, with the tone "See, it's like this, right?" Used among friends.

ja-nai-q.note: The tone rises at the end of the sentence, and it confirms with the listener or offers your own view. It is not a negation.
ja-nai-q.translation: That's a bit strange, isn't it?

kamo.note: Spoken form of 「かもしれない」, cut short.

kana.note: A guess or hesitation said to yourself. Said to others, it is softer than asking directly.
kana.translation: I wonder if it will rain.

you-kana.note: Says what you plan to do but have not fully decided.

yo-ne.note: States your view and at the same time wants the other person to agree.

n-da-kedo.note: Explains the situation first and often leaves out the rest, so the listener understands. Very common for requests and asking advice.
n-da-kedo.translation: I do want to go, but...

toka.note: Gives examples, or makes the wording vague so it is not too definite. 「AとかBとか」 gives several examples.
toka.translation: I'd like to watch a movie or something.

nanka.note: A vague word in speech. At the start of a sentence it means "somehow", and after a noun it means "things like ..." (sometimes with contempt).

tatte.translation: Even if you run now, you won't make it.

datte-even.note: Spoken form of 「でも」: even something like this ....

ssu.note: The 「です」 that young people or men use to seniors, between polite and casual.

tte-iu-ka.note: Corrects what was just said, or changes the subject. Spoken.

ba-ii.note: Asks what to do, or gives advice. 「〜たらいい」 and 「〜といい」 mean almost the same.

ba-noni.note: Things did not go that way, and the speaker feels regret or complains.
ba-noni.translation: If only you had come earlier.

buri-ni.note: Does something again after a long gap.
buri-ni.translation: I returned to my country after three years.

chuu.note: Follows a noun, showing it is in progress, or within this period (今日中, 午前中).
chuu.translation: We are in a meeting now.

furi-wo-suru.note: It is not actually so, but someone acts as if it were.

goto-ni.note: At every interval, or for each one.
goto-ni.translation: The Olympics are held every four years.

donnani-temo.note: Stresses that the result does not change no matter how far it goes.
donnani-temo.translation: No matter how hard I tried, I couldn't win.

kekka.note: After doing the front thing, the back result was obtained.
kekka.translation: As a result of the discussion, it was cancelled.

kiru.note: Follows a verb ます stem and shows it is done thoroughly. 「〜切れない」 means cannot finish.
kiru.translation: I read the whole book in one night.

koto-wa-ga.note: Admits the front first, then adds a not-so-good point. The same word is used before and after.
koto-wa-ga.translation: I do go, but I'll be late.

marude.translation: It is just like a dream.

kesshite.note: A strong denial, often showing determination.

moshikashitara.note: 「もしかしたら」 and 「もしかすると」 are often used with 「かもしれない」 for a guess with a low chance.

n-datte.note: Spoken, reports what you heard. With a rising tone at the end it asks "I hear ...?".
n-datte.translation: I hear he is getting married.

ni-nareru.note: Something no longer feels strange or hard.
ni-nareru.translation: I got used to life in Japan.

ni-wa-purpose.meaning: if you want to ...; in order to ...
ni-wa-purpose.note: Follows a verb dictionary form and shows purpose. What comes after says what is needed or what is better.
ni-wa-purpose.translation: If you want to go to the station, the bus is handy.

sou-mo-nai.meaning: does not look like it will ...
sou-mo-nai.note: Judging from the situation, there is almost no chance.
sou-mo-nai.translation: It doesn't look like I can finish it today.

te-goran.note: A gentle form of 「〜てみなさい」, said to children or juniors.

te-hajimete.note: Only after experiencing something do you understand or manage it for the first time.
te-hajimete.translation: I understood the value of health only after I got sick.

te-sumu.note: A simple method like this solves it, and no more is needed.
te-sumu.translation: If a phone call is enough, I don't need to go.

te-iru-baai.note: The situation is urgent and there is no time to do this.

temo-hajimaranai.note: Doing it will not change anything.
temo-hajimaranai.translation: It is no use regretting it now.

temo-kamawanai.note: Shows permission, a little more formal than 「〜てもいい」.

temo-shouganai.note: Doing it will not lead to a result. Spoken.

to-ii.meaning: I hope ...; it would be good if ...
to-ii.note: Expresses a wish, or gives advice to the other person.
to-ii.translation: I hope you get well soon.

to-mieru.note: A guess from what you see.
to-mieru.translation: He seems tired, and fell asleep right away.

tochuu.meaning: on the way to ...; in the middle of ...
tochuu.note: While moving or doing something that is not finished yet.
tochuu.translation: I met my teacher on the way to school.

to-wa-kagiranai.note: People generally think so, but there are exceptions.
to-wa-kagiranai.translation: Expensive things are not necessarily good.

tsumori-datta.note: The original plan did not come true.
tsumori-datta.translation: I was going to go, but I couldn't.

you-na-ki-ga-suru.note: There is no basis, it is just a feeling.
you-na-ki-ga-suru.translation: I feel as if I have seen it somewhere.

you-to-shinai.note: Someone does not want to do it, and the speaker is unhappy about it.

zutsu.note: Follows an amount, and shows an equal share or the same amount repeated.
zutsu.translation: Please come in one at a time.

darake.translation: My clothes are covered with mud.

gimi.note: Slightly has this feeling or tendency, mostly a bad one.
gimi.translation: I have a bit of a cold lately.

koto-kara.note: Explains the grounds or cause of a judgment or a name.
koto-kara.translation: From the footprints, we know the criminal came in through the window.

koto-ni-natte-iru.meaning: is supposed to ...; the rule is ...
koto-ni-natte-iru.note: A rule, a custom or an arrangement already made.
koto-ni-natte-iru.translation: By company rule, work starts at nine in the morning.

kurai.note: After an amount it means "about". After a verb or adjective it means "to the extent that ...".
kurai.translation: I'm so sad I could cry.

ni-hanshite.note: The result differs from what was expected or hoped.
ni-hanshite.translation: Contrary to expectations, we lost the match.

kara-ni-kakete.note: Shows a rough range of time or place.
kara-ni-kakete.translation: It will rain from tonight into tomorrow.

ni-oite.translation: The meeting is held in Tokyo.

ni-shitagatte.note: Follows a rule or instruction, or as one side changes, the other changes too.

ni-tsurete.note: As one side changes, the other changes too.
ni-tsurete.translation: As we get older, our bodies weaken.

wo-chuushin-ni.note: Has something as the center or focus.
wo-chuushin-ni.translation: The town spreads out around the station.

wo-komete.note: Puts feelings or heart into it.
wo-komete.translation: I wrote the letter with all my heart.

wo-tsuujite.note: Shows a means or go-between, or the whole period.

sai-ni.note: Formal form of 「とき」, often used in notices.
sai-ni.translation: When you leave, please do not forget your belongings.

tatoe-temo.note: Imagines a case, and the result will not change.
tatoe-temo.translation: I'll go even if it rains.

te-kara-denai-to.note: You must finish the front thing first before you can do the back thing.
te-kara-denai-to.translation: You can't play until you finish your homework.

to-iu-koto-da.note: Reports news you heard, or sums up what was said before.
to-iu-koto-da.translation: I hear tomorrow is a day off.

to-iu-to.note: Brings up a topic and says what it makes you think of.
to-iu-to.translation: Speaking of Japan, you think of Mt. Fuji.

to-iu-yori.note: Switches to a more accurate way of saying it.
to-iu-yori.translation: He is more like a friend than a teacher.

to-itte-mo.note: Admits the front, but the actual level is lower than you would imagine.
to-itte-mo.translation: I can cook, but only simple things.

to-shitara.note: Imagines a case and thinks about it.
to-shitara.translation: If you won the lottery, what would you do?

to-tomo-ni.note: Written style. Do something together, or as one side changes, the other changes at the same time.
to-tomo-ni.translation: I live together with my family.

ue-ni.note: Adds one more thing (in the same direction) on top of the front.
ue-ni.translation: This room is not only spacious but also bright.

wa-betsu-to-shite.translation: Price aside, the design is nice.

bakari-de-naku.note: Same as 「だけでなく」 but a little more written.
bakari-de-naku.translation: He can speak not only English but also Chinese.

ageku.note: After a long time or much trouble, the final (mostly bad) result.
ageku.translation: After hesitating for a long time, I didn't buy it in the end.

amari.note: A feeling or state was so strong that it led to an unusual result.
amari.translation: I was so worried that I couldn't sleep.

ijou-wa.note: Since things have come to this, of course you take responsibility.
ijou-wa.translation: Since I promised, I must keep it.

ippou-de.meaning: on the one hand ..., on the other ...
ippou-de.note: Contrasts two sides of the same thing.
ippou-de.translation: He is capable at work, but on the other hand neglects his family.

you-dewa-nai-ka.note: Calls on everyone to do it together. Used in speeches and writing. In speech it is 「〜（よ）うじゃないか」.

eru.note: It is possible. The negative is 「〜得ない」 (impossible).
eru.translation: Such a thing can happen, too.

kagiri.note: Within this condition or range (as far as I know, as long as it still ...).
kagiri.translation: As far as I know, he is an honest person.

ka-nai-ka-no-uchi-ni.note: The second thing happens almost before the first is finished.
ka-nai-ka-no-uchi-ni.translation: The bell had barely rung when he left the classroom.

kaneru.note: A polite refusal: you cannot because of your position and so on. Note that it differs from 「〜かねない」.
kaneru.translation: I find it hard to agree with your opinion.

kara-iu-to.note: Judges from a certain position or viewpoint.
kara-iu-to.translation: From an expert's viewpoint, this method is dangerous.

kara-shite.note: Names one point as the grounds for a judgment.
kara-shite.translation: Judging from that attitude, he is not reflecting.

kara-suru-to.translation: Judging from the way he speaks, he must be from Kansai.

kara-to-itte.note: You cannot conclude from this reason alone, and a negative usually follows.
kara-to-itte.translation: Just because he is rich doesn't mean he is happy.

kara-ni-wa.note: Since things are already this way, you must see it through.
kara-ni-wa.translation: Now that I promised, I will surely keep it.

kara-miru-to.translation: From a child's point of view, adults are sly.

kawari-ni.note: Something else takes its place, or "while getting ..., also ...".
kawari-ni.translation: My younger brother goes instead of me.

ge.note: Follows an adjective stem and shows it looks like it has this feeling.

koto-ka.note: A strong exclamation, often with 「どんなに」 or 「何度」.

koto-da-kara.note: A guess based on what you know about the person.
koto-da-kara.translation: That person will surely be late again.

koto-naku.note: Written style. Never once does this thing.
koto-naku.translation: He works without a moment's rest.

shidai-de.note: Things change according to the front condition.
shidai-de.translation: We will change the plan depending on the result.

jou.note: Follows a noun and means "in the matter of ...".

dake-ni.note: Because of the front situation, the feeling behind is stronger.
dake-ni.translation: Because I practiced so hard, losing is all the more frustrating.

ta-tokoro.note: After doing something, I found the result behind.
ta-tokoro.translation: When I asked the teacher, I heard tomorrow is a holiday.

tsutsu-aru.note: Written style. A change is going on little by little.
tsutsu-aru.translation: The environment is gradually getting worse.

te-irai.note: Has continued from then until now.
te-irai.translation: Since coming to Japan, I have lived in Tokyo.

to-iu-mono-da.note: States a general truth or the speaker's view.
to-iu-mono-da.translation: Helping a friend is what friendship is.

to-iu-mono-dewa-nai.translation: It's not just a matter of having money.

dokoroka.meaning: far from ... (not even ...); on the contrary
dokoroka.note: The real situation is very far from what was just said.
dokoroka.translation: I'm so busy that, far from resting, I don't even have time to sleep.

dokoro-dewa-nai.meaning: no time to ...; out of the question
dokoro-dewa-nai.note: The present situation does not allow this.
dokoro-dewa-nai.translation: I'm so busy that traveling is out of the question.

tokoro-ni.note: While doing something, another thing happens (often an interruption).
tokoro-ni.translation: Just as I was about to go out, a phone call came.

nai-koto-ni-wa.note: Without doing this first, the next thing is not possible.
nai-koto-ni-wa.translation: You won't know unless you try.

ni-atatte.note: Before or during something important. Written style.
ni-atatte.translation: He gave a speech at the opening.

ni-oujite.note: Changes accordingly as the front situation changes.
ni-oujite.translation: Taxes are paid according to income.

ni-kagitte.note: Only this one is special (won't do this / of all times).
ni-kagitte.translation: Only my child would never do such a thing.

ni-kakete-wa.note: In this field the ability is greatest and nobody can match it.
ni-kakete-wa.translation: When it comes to cooking, nobody can match him.

ni-kuwaete.note: Adds the back thing on top of the front.
ni-kuwaete.translation: In addition to the rain, the wind has picked up.

ni-kotaete.note: Answers other people's hopes or demands.
ni-kotaete.translation: In response to the fans' calls, he sang another song.

ni-saishite.note: When doing something special. Written style.
ni-saishite.translation: At the time of departure, the precautions are explained.

ni-sakidatte.note: Before something starts, you do the preparing thing first.
ni-sakidatte.translation: An opening ceremony was held before the match.

ni-shitara.translation: For parents, children are always a worry.

ni-tsuke.note: Whenever this kind of thing happens, it always ....

ni-tomonatte.note: As one side changes, the other changes too. Written style.
ni-tomonatte.translation: As the population grows, problems also increase.

ni-hoka-naranai.translation: That is nothing other than the result of effort.

ni-watatte.note: The time or range is long or wide.
ni-watatte.translation: The meeting lasted for three days.

nuki.note: Removes something or does not count it.
nuki.translation: Joking aside, it was really hard.

nuku.note: Follows a verb ます stem and shows you keep going to the end.
nuku.translation: I ran all the way to the end.

no-sue.note: After a long effort or much thought, a result is reached.
no-sue.translation: After much thought, I finally resigned.

nomi-narazu.translation: He can speak not only English but also Chinese.

no-moto-de.note: Under someone's guidance, influence or conditions.
no-moto-de.translation: The research goes forward under the teacher's guidance.

hanmen.note: The same thing has a good side and an opposite side.
hanmen.translation: Along with its convenience, there is also danger.

hoka-nai.note: There is no other way, so you do this. Close to 「しかない」.
hoka-nai.translation: I had no choice but to do it.

mai.note: Written form of a negative will ("never ...") or a negative guess ("probably will not ...").
mai.translation: I don't think I'll ever go again.

muki.note: Just right for a certain kind of person or use. 「向け」 means made specially for ....

mo-ba-mo.note: Names two things of the same kind and stresses that both apply.

mo-kamawazu.note: Does not mind what ordinary people would mind.
mo-kamawazu.translation: He talks loudly without caring about the trouble to others.

mono-ga-aru.note: A certain quality the speaker feels in something.
mono-ga-aru.translation: There is something attractive about his words.

mono-da-kara.note: Explains a reason, often used to excuse oneself.
mono-da-kara.translation: The road was jammed, so I was late.

mono-nara.note: Imagines something that is hard to realize. After the volitional form it means "if ... (something bad will follow)".
mono-nara.translation: If you can do it, go ahead and try.

yara.note: Names several examples and shows there are many things, all mixed up.
yara.translation: What with cleaning and washing, I'm busy.

wo-to-shite.note: Treats someone or something as a certain status or purpose.
wo-to-shite.translation: Let him take part in the meeting as a representative.

wo-kikkake-ni.note: Because of something, a new change begins.
wo-kikkake-ni.translation: I quit smoking when I was hospitalized.

wo-keiki-ni.note: Written form of 「をきっかけに」.
wo-keiki-ni.translation: We bought a house when we got married.

wo-towazu.note: Has nothing to do with this condition.
wo-towazu.translation: Anyone can take part regardless of age.

wo-megutte.note: A dispute or discussion develops around some issue.
wo-megutte.translation: A quarrel broke out over the inheritance.

ikan.note: Written style. The matter depends on what comes before. 「いかんにかかわらず」 means "regardless of ...".
ikan.translation: Depending on the result, the plan may be stopped.

you-ga-mai-ga.note: Whether it is so or not, the result is the same.
you-ga-mai-ga.translation: Rain or shine, the match goes ahead.

you-ni-mo-nai.note: You want to do it but for some reason cannot. The same verb is often used before and after.
you-ni-mo-nai.translation: It hurts so much I can't move even if I wanted to.

kagiri-da.note: Follows a feeling adjective and shows the feeling is very strong.
kagiri-da.translation: I'm extremely happy to meet you.

ga-saigo.note: Once you do this, the (mostly bad) result behind will surely follow.
ga-saigo.translation: Once he falls asleep, he won't wake up until morning.

katagata.note: While doing one thing, also do another. Written style, mostly used for visits and greetings.
katagata.translation: I dropped by a bookstore while taking a walk.

katawara.note: While doing the main job, you also do another thing for a long time.
katawara.translation: He writes novels besides working at a company.

gatera.note: While doing something, you also do another. More spoken than 「かたがた」.
gatera.translation: I bought bread while on a walk.

kara-aru.note: Stresses that the amount is large.
kara-aru.translation: I carried luggage weighing as much as fifty kilograms.

kirai-ga-aru.note: Has a bad tendency or habit. Written style.
kirai-ga-aru.translation: He has a habit of exaggerating when he talks.

kiwamari-nai.note: Written style. The degree is very high, mostly for bad things.

gotoku.note: Written form of 「ように」 and 「ような」.
gotoku.translation: He got angry like a demon.

koto-tote.note: Written style. Explains the reason, often used to apologize or ask for forgiveness.
koto-tote.translation: He is only a child, so please forgive him.

koto-nashi-ni.note: Without doing the front thing, the back thing cannot come true.
koto-nashi-ni.translation: Without effort there is no success.

shimatsu.note: Things got worse and worse, and finally ended in this bad result.
shimatsu.translation: In the end, my younger brother even ran away from home.

zu-ni-wa-sumanai.note: By social common sense or by the situation, it would not be right not to do it.
zu-ni-wa-sumanai.translation: You can't get away without apologizing for this responsibility.

tada-nomi.note: Written style. Same as 「ただ〜だけ」.
tada-nomi.translation: All that's left is to pray.

ta-tokoro-de.note: Even if you do it, you won't get the result you hoped for.
ta-tokoro-de.translation: Even if you go now, you won't make it.

dani.note: Written style. 「想像だにしない」, 「考えるだに恐ろしい」.
dani.translation: I never even imagined such a thing.

taritomo.note: Follows 「一」 + a counter and stresses not even one.
taritomo.translation: I have not rested even a single day.

taru.note: Written style. Stresses how someone in that status should be.
taru.translation: As a teacher, you must be fair to your students.

tsu-tsu.translation: It was a match in which they chased each other.

de-are.note: Whatever the situation, the conclusion is the same.
de-are.translation: Whatever the reason, violence is not acceptable.

te-kara-to-iu-mono.note: Using something as a dividing line, the situation has changed completely since.
te-kara-to-iu-mono.translation: Since I came to Japan, I have been busy every day.

to-aimatte.note: Two factors work together and the effect is stronger.
to-aimatte.translation: Combined with the good weather, there were many customers.

to-ii-to-ii.note: Names several points and says it is so for all.
to-ii-to-ii.translation: Both in taste and in price, this shop is the best.

to-iu-tokoro-da.note: At most it is about this level.
to-iu-tokoro-da.translation: It is right about at the passing line.

to-iedomo.note: Written style. Even someone or something like this ....
to-iedomo.translation: Even though he is a child, he has responsibility.

to-omoikiya.note: The result is the opposite of what was expected.
to-omoikiya.translation: I thought I had passed, but I hadn't.

to-kitara.note: Brings up a topic, and dissatisfaction or criticism usually follows. Spoken.
to-kitara.translation: As for my husband, he does nothing.

to-shitatte.note: Spoken form of 「としても」 and 「にしても」.
to-shitatte.translation: Even if you beg now, it won't work.

to-wa-surprise.note: Shows surprise at something unexpected, and the rest is often left out.
to-wa-surprise.translation: To think we would meet in a place like this.

to-wa-ie.note: Admits the front, but the real situation is different.
to-wa-ie.translation: Although it is spring, it is still cold.

to-bakari-ni.note: It is not said aloud, but the attitude means exactly this.
to-bakari-ni.translation: As if he had been waiting for this moment, he started to talk.

tomo-naku.note: Did it without doing it on purpose.
tomo-naku.translation: I overheard the conversation without meaning to.

nai-made-mo.note: You cannot reach the front level, but you should at least do the back.
nai-made-mo.translation: Even if you can't pay it all, at least pay half.

nai-mono-demo-nai.meaning: it is not that one cannot ...
nai-mono-demo-nai.note: There is a little chance, but not eager.
nai-mono-demo-nai.translation: It's not that I can't go.

nakushite.note: Written style. Without the front thing, the back cannot hold.
nakushite.translation: Without effort there is no success.

nashi-ni.note: Did not do what should have been done.
nashi-ni.translation: You can't get in without a reservation.

narade-wa.note: A characteristic that only this place or person can have.
narade-wa.translation: This is a dish unique to Kyoto.

nari-nari.note: Gives examples and lets the other person choose.
nari-nari.translation: Please contact us by phone or email.

nari-ni.note: Does as much as possible according to one's own ability or position.
nari-ni.translation: Children have their own ideas too.

ni-wa-ataranai.note: It is not necessary to do so.
ni-wa-ataranai.translation: There's no need to be surprised.

ni-atte.note: Written style. In this special time or position.

ni-itaru-made.note: The range goes up to here, stressing everything.
ni-itaru-made.translation: I did everything from small matters to big ones.

ni-kakawaru.note: Linked to an important matter, mostly a serious one.
ni-kakawaru.translation: It is a matter that affects life.

ni-shite.note: Written style. Only at this stage ...; or "even ...".
ni-shite.translation: He married for the first time at forty.

ni-sokushite.note: Acts in line with facts, rules and so on.
ni-sokushite.translation: Judge in line with the facts.

ni-taenai.note: So bad that you cannot bear to look or listen.
ni-taenai.translation: It is too terrible to look at.

ni-taru.note: Written style. Has enough value to do it.

ni-hikikae.note: Compares two things that differ a lot.
ni-hikikae.translation: Unlike his older brother, the younger brother is hardworking.

ni-mo-mashite.note: Compared with others, this is more ....
ni-mo-mashite.translation: More important than anything is health.

no-itari.note: Written style. A feeling reaches its peak.

no-kiwami.note: Written style. Reaches the highest degree.
no-kiwami.translation: It is the height of luxury.

wa-oroka.note: The front is of course so, and even the simpler one ....
wa-oroka.translation: Let alone kanji, I can't even write hiragana.

ba-koso.translation: It is precisely because I love you that I scold you.

ba-sore-made.note: If this happens, everything is over and nothing can be done.
ba-sore-made.translation: If you fail, it's all over.

bekarazu.note: A written prohibition, often seen on notices.

beku.note: Written style. To reach a certain goal. する becomes 「すべく」.
beku.translation: To pass the exam, I study every day.

majiki.note: Written style. Something that, given the status, absolutely must not be done.

made-da.note: There is no other way, so just do this; or "it is merely ...".
made-da.translation: If it doesn't work, at worst I'll quit.

ya-inaya.note: Written style. The first thing has just happened and the second follows at once.
ya-inaya.translation: As soon as it started to rain, I bought an umbrella.

yue.note: Written form of 「から」 and 「ために」.
yue.translation: Because of poverty, he could not go on to higher school.

wo-oite.note: Besides this person or thing, nothing suits better. A negative mostly follows.
wo-oite.translation: Apart from him, there is no suitable person.

wo-kagiri-ni.note: Up to this time, and never again after.

wo-motte.note: Written style. Shows a means or a time limit.

yogi-naku.note: Written style. Forced to do so because of outside reasons.

wo-yoso-ni.note: Pays no attention to the worry or opposition around.
wo-yoso-ni.translation: He went out, ignoring the worry of people around him.

n-ga-tame.note: Written style. To reach this goal at any cost.
n-ga-tame.translation: To win, I kept on practicing.

mo-saru-koto-nagara.note: The front is of course important, and the back is just as important or more.
mo-saru-koto-nagara.translation: Taste goes without saying, and the atmosphere of the shop is nice too.

de-nakute-nan.note: A written emphasis: this is exactly ....
de-nakute-nan.translation: What is this if not a miracle?

ga-suru.meaning: there is ... (a sound, taste or smell)
ga-suru.note: You sense a sound, taste, smell and so on. 「気がする」 means "I feel that ...".

garu.note: When telling what other people feel, add がる after an adjective. It is not used for yourself.

janai-ka.note: Checks with the other person, or shows surprise or blame. Stronger than a plain question.

kashira.note: Doubt or a guess said to yourself. Mostly used by women.
kashira.translation: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.

kai.note: A friendly or casual question, mostly used by men.

koro.translation: When I was little, I often swam.

oki-ni.note: Repeats after a gap of time or distance. 「一日おきに」 means every other day.

te-yokatta.note: Things turned out this way, and you feel glad or relieved.
te-yokatta.translation: I'm glad I made it in time.

to-iwarete-iru.translation: It is said that this medicine works well.

to-kiita.translation: I heard he is getting married next month.

yotei.note: A plan that has already been set. More definite than 「つもり」.
yotei.translation: I'm scheduled to go to Tokyo tomorrow.

made-ni.note: A deadline: finish before this time. 「まで」 means it continues until then.
made-ni.translation: Please come back by five o'clock.

nakanaka-nai.note: You want to do it but find it hard, or it does not happen for a long time.

ni-mieru.note: It looks like this from the outside.

o-kudasai.note: An honorific form of 「〜てください」.

no-wa-da.note: Puts the part you want to stress at the back.

baai-wa.translation: If it rains, we will cancel.

hitsuyou-ga-aru.meaning: need to ...; it is necessary to ...
